brief.headline: Ask for ₹32.69 L/yr back by matching the ₹290.00/KG we already pay, and push 15-day faster payment in return for a price cut of about 4.38%

priceAsk.summary: Bring their laminate price down to ₹290.00/KG across all three big SKUs
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹290.00/KG to Shrinath Roto Pack Pvt Ltd for the same laminates — GEEP charges us ₹294.03/KG to ₹308.30/KG on the top items, 1.4% to 6.3% more. Market research shows pharma ORS sachets trade at ₹205–305/kg (typical ₹250/kg), so ₹290.00/KG sits at the top of fair range and is defensible.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 Days After Receipt to 15 Days After Receipt, and give us a price cut of roughly 4.38% in return
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹1.16 Cr of our cash, but their cash is stuck for 81 days (longer than the 46d norm), so early payment is worth about 4.38% per year to them — trade that saving for a matching price drop

brief.financialLeverage: GEEP brings in ₹291.36 Cr a year and we account for ₹28.31 Cr of it — 9.72% of everything they sell — so losing us would sting. They keep only 1.1% as profit (half the 2.1% that similar firms keep), so there's not much room for a big price cut without hurting them. Their cash is stuck for 81 days versus 46d at peer firms, meaning they feel the pinch when customers pay late; offering to pay 15 days earlier (worth roughly 4.38% a year to them) is a strong lever. They stopped sharing information with CRISIL (rating is BB+ / Stable but done without their help), and they've had GST filing delays, EPF payment delays and pending legal cases — so treat their financial picture as uncertain and keep a backup ready.

evidence.point: We spend 9.72% of their total sales
They keep only 1.1% profit on every ₹100 they sell, half the 2.1% peer level
Their cash is stuck for 81 days, much longer than similar firms at 46 days
Paying 15 days faster is worth roughly 4.38% a year to them
We overpay ₹32.69 L a year versus the ₹290.00/KG we already get from Shrinath
Rating agency did the BB+ / Stable rating without GEEP's help, and they have GST filing delays, EPF payment delays and legal cases pending
evidence.figure: CRISIL BB+ / Stable (issuerNotCooperating: true); riskFlags: GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, Pending legal case(s)

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: A listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC in small volume — proven and scalable for laminate sachets; a strong second source to qualify

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: A listed flexibles giant that makes both the film substrate and does conversion — can second-source GEEP at scale; a lead to qualify (verify before RFQ)

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of the global Constantia group, focuses on pharma blister and sachet laminates — a strong second-source lead to qualify (verify before RFQ)

risks: GEEP supplies 76% of our laminates (₹28.31 Cr) — we have no approved backup, so pushing too hard risks our supply; qualify Huhtamaki or UFLEX fast
Their profit is only 1.1% — a steep price cut could tip them into loss and threaten continuity; focus the ask on matching our existing ₹290.00/KG price and trading faster payment for a rate cut
CRISIL rated them BB+ / Stable without their cooperation, and they have GST, EPF and legal issues — their real financial state is unclear, so keep the second source plan front and center
Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹1.16 Cr of our cash — make sure the price cut we get in return (about 4.38%) is locked in writing and doesn't evaporate after a few months
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹294 to ₹308 per kilo when we already get the same laminate at ₹290 — let's close that gap and talk about how paying you faster can help both of us.
